definition: A clustering algorithm that partitions data into k groups by iteratively assigning points to the nearest cluster center and updating cluster centers.
details: K-means is one of the most widely used clustering algorithms due to its simplicity and efficiency, though it requires specifying the number of clusters in advance and assumes roughly spherical cluster shapes.
story: Imagine a chef tasting every ingredient before it goes into the pot, deciding what belongs and what would ruin the broth. Better ingredients make a better meal, and the same is true here. Every machine is shaped by what it was shown, so someone has to choose that material with care. It is the raw material; the model is only ever as good as what it was fed. That care with the raw material is K-Means Clustering.
